description: Evidence ledger for the own parts: one entry per id a part cites. Claims are own-words paraphrases with ranges, never code, third-party identifiers or a named defect. Labels: measured, documented, inferred, policy. Sources are public URLs or 'local benchmark' (measured on synthetic media in headless browsers). Re-measuring is by hand only. sourceSha is the SHA-256 of the private finding or notes section the entry was written from, checked by scripts/import-findings.mjs --check <research folder>.

AM-7.claim: Large product sites keep motion durations in design tokens and switch reduced motion by zeroing those tokens in one override block instead of guarding each rule.
AM-7.value: duration tokens set to 0 under reduced motion
AM-7.label: measured
AM-7.method: Read the published stylesheets of public product pages by hand and counted motion tokens and their overrides.
AM-7.remeasure: Open a product page's stylesheet in a browser's developer tools and look for duration custom properties and their reduced-motion overrides.

AM-10.claim: Scroll progress maps linearly to keyframes; any smoothing applied as a fixed fraction per animation frame converges at a speed that depends on the display's refresh rate.
AM-10.value: per-frame smoothing settles about twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz
AM-10.label: measured
AM-10.method: Read the public scroll library of product pages by hand and computed the convergence of its per-frame smoothing at two refresh rates.
AM-10.remeasure: Compute how many frames a per-frame factor needs to reach 95 percent and convert at 60 and 120 Hz.

AM-12.claim: A pinned scene is a tall box holding a sticky child the height of the viewport; the box is the scene's travel plus one viewport height.
AM-12.value: box = travel + 100vh; sticky child 100vh, lvh or svh; travel 70-300vh
AM-12.label: measured
AM-12.method: Read the published stylesheets of public product pages by hand and recorded box heights and sticky offsets.
AM-12.remeasure: Inspect a pinned section in developer tools: its height, the sticky child's height and top.
AM-12.correction: The re-check put measured travel at 70-300vh, not the first reading of 150-400vh.

AM-13.claim: Scroll choreography sits behind one capability decision: reduced motion, a viewport too short for the stage and a rejected muted autoplay probe each leave the static layout in place.
AM-13.value: static layout when any gate fails
AM-13.label: measured
AM-13.method: Read the public page scripts by hand and listed the conditions that keep the static layout.
AM-13.remeasure: Load a product page with reduced motion on, then in a short window, and compare the layouts.
AM-13.correction: The re-check kept reduced motion, short viewports and the muted play probe as the general gates; other page-specific gates are context only.

AM-16.claim: Blocked autoplay and iOS Low Power Mode are detected by trying to play a tiny muted inline clip at start-up; a rejection keeps the static layout.
AM-16.value: a rejected muted play() keeps the static layout
AM-16.label: measured
AM-16.method: Read the public page scripts by hand.
AM-16.remeasure: Turn on Low Power Mode on an iPhone and load a product page with a scrubbed film.

AM-17.claim: Scroll-scrubbed product films map scroll progress straight to the video's current time without smoothing, prime decoding with a play that is paused at once, and fall back to a still after a load timeout.
AM-17.value: progress to currentTime without smoothing; a load timeout falls back to a still
AM-17.label: measured
AM-17.method: Read the public page scripts by hand.
AM-17.remeasure: Watch a scrubbed film's currentTime in developer tools while scrolling.

AM-19.claim: Inline and scrub product films share one baseline: H.264 High, yuv420p, bt709 primaries with an sRGB transfer tag, no audio track and the moov box first.
AM-19.value: H.264 High; yuv420p; bt709 with an sRGB transfer tag; no audio; moov first
AM-19.label: measured
AM-19.method: Read public media files with ffprobe and an MP4 box reader.
AM-19.remeasure: Run ffprobe on a downloaded product film and read its codec, pixel format, colour tags and streams.
AM-19.correction: The re-check found one recent page that ships only AV1 and VP9 files, so the baseline is common, not universal.

AM-23.claim: Under reduced motion product pages jump to end states, zero their durations, keep content visible and show a still instead of autoplaying decorative video.
AM-23.value: end states; durations 0; still instead of decorative autoplay
AM-23.label: measured
AM-23.method: Read the published stylesheets and scripts by hand.
AM-23.remeasure: Load a product page with reduced motion on and compare it with the default.

SC-1.claim: Scrub films ship with short GOPs, a keyframe every 2 to 8 frames with B-frames allowed, rather than all-intra; an HEVC scrub file uses the hvc1 sample entry.
SC-1.value: a keyframe every 2-8 frames; hvc1 for HEVC
SC-1.label: measured
SC-1.method: Read the sync-sample tables of public scrub films with an MP4 box reader.
SC-1.remeasure: List keyframes with ffprobe -show_entries packet=flags on a downloaded scrub film.

SC-2.claim: Product sites pick the scrub file per browser and load it fully before scrubbing, with a load timeout that falls back to a still.
SC-2.value: full load before scrubbing; a 10 s load timeout
SC-2.label: measured
SC-2.method: Read the public page scripts by hand.
SC-2.remeasure: Throttle the network in developer tools and watch when the film appears.

SC-4.claim: The film starts loading well before its scene, sits over a start image, is primed with a play that is paused at once, and is revealed only once loaded.
SC-4.value: load 150-250vh ahead; start image underneath; reveal after loading
SC-4.label: measured
SC-4.method: Read the public page scripts and stylesheets by hand.
SC-4.remeasure: Watch the network panel while scrolling towards a scrubbed scene.
SC-4.correction: The re-check widened the load window to 150-250vh.

SC-7.claim: A closed GOP of 6 frames scrubs as smoothly as all-intra on hardware decode for about a third of the bytes, while a default long GOP drops about half the frames of a sweep.
SC-7.value: GOP 6 kept every frame of a sweep; all-intra about 2.9 times the bytes of GOP 6; a default long GOP showed about half
SC-7.label: measured
SC-7.method: Encoded one synthetic clip at several GOP lengths and swept it in headless Chromium and WebKit, counting distinct presented frames.
SC-7.remeasure: Encode a clip at GOP 6 and at the encoder default, sweep both and count presented frames with requestVideoFrameCallback.

SC-8.claim: Writing currentTime on every animation frame starves the decoder; a latest-wins queue that writes only when the element is not seeking keeps frames flowing.
SC-8.value: naive writes presented a small fraction of the frames a latest-wins queue presented
SC-8.label: measured
SC-8.method: Swept long-GOP and short-GOP clips in headless Chromium with both driving strategies and counted presented frames.
SC-8.remeasure: Drive one clip both ways for 2 s and count presented frames.

SC-9.claim: An HEVC encode with the encoder's default open GOP lands seeks on the wrong frame; a closed GOP fixes it at the same size.
SC-9.value: open GOP: wrong frames on many seeks; closed GOP: none
SC-9.label: measured
SC-9.method: Seeked to frame centres in headless Chromium and WebKit and compared the presented frame with the request.
SC-9.remeasure: Encode HEVC with and without a closed GOP and compare requested and presented frames.

SC-10.claim: Without an explicit yuv420p pixel format a 4:4:4 master encodes to a 4:4:4 profile that Chromium decodes on a slow path.
SC-10.label: measured
SC-10.method: Encoded one master with and without a 4:2:0 conversion and measured seek times in headless Chromium.
SC-10.remeasure: Encode a 4:4:4 master without -pix_fmt yuv420p and read the profile with ffprobe.

SC-11.claim: At matched quality an image sequence costs several times the bytes of GOP-6 video.
SC-11.value: 2.3-5.3 times the bytes of GOP-6 video
SC-11.label: measured
SC-11.method: Encoded one synthetic clip as video and as AVIF, WebP and JPEG sequences and compared sizes at equal VMAF.
SC-11.remeasure: Compare a sequence and a GOP-6 encode of the same clip at equal VMAF.
SC-11.correction: A re-check on other content measured about 1.95 times, so quote 1.95-5.3 times by content.

SC-12.claim: Each decoded frame of an image sequence holds width x height x 4 bytes, and per-frame decode takes milliseconds, so a full sequence at high resolution can need gigabytes of memory.
SC-12.value: frames x width x height x 4 bytes decoded
SC-12.label: measured
SC-12.method: Timed createImageBitmap in headless Chromium and WebKit and computed decoded sizes.
SC-12.remeasure: Multiply frames by width, height and 4 for the planned sequence.

SC-14.claim: Behind a server that ignores byte-range requests Chromium marks the video unseekable and currentTime stays at 0; a Blob URL made with fetch makes it seekable whatever the server does.
SC-14.value: without 206 Range responses: unseekable; a Blob URL: seekable
SC-14.label: measured
SC-14.method: Served one clip with and without Range support to headless Chromium and seeked it; Apple's Safari web content guide requires byte-range support for media on iOS.
SC-14.remeasure: Request the first 100 bytes with curl --range 0-99 and check for a 206 answer.

SC-15.claim: The preload attribute cannot be relied on to buffer a whole film, and seeking into unbuffered ranges stalls on the network.
SC-15.value: load the whole film in a scroll-ahead window
SC-15.label: measured
SC-15.method: Measured seeks into unbuffered ranges in headless Chromium; preload behaviour is documented on web.dev.
SC-15.remeasure: Seek a plain-src film to its end right after load and time it.

SC-16.claim: An MP4 with the moov box at the end costs an extra range request before metadata, or a full download without range support.
SC-16.label: measured
SC-16.method: Served faststart and moov-at-end files to headless Chromium and logged the requests before metadata.
SC-16.remeasure: List the top-level boxes of the file and check that moov comes before mdat.

SC-17.claim: Safari's fastSeek() snaps to keyframes, so it lands on the wrong frame for scrubbing unless every frame is a keyframe.
SC-17.value: fastSeek() wrong on most seeks with GOP 6; never use it
SC-17.label: measured
SC-17.method: Seeked a GOP-6 clip with fastSeek() in WebKit and compared presented frames; support data from MDN.
SC-17.remeasure: Call fastSeek() to random frame centres in Safari and compare presented frames.

SC-21.claim: iOS Low Power Mode blocks autoplay of muted inline video, which also stalls scrub players; a rejected play() is the practical signal.
SC-21.value: a rejected muted play() means no scrubbing
SC-21.label: documented
SC-21.method: Community reports; no WebKit statement was found.
SC-21.remeasure: Turn on Low Power Mode on an iPhone and call play() on a muted inline video.

SC-22.claim: Codec support differs by browser and decoder: Chromium without hardware decode cannot play HEVC at all, and VP9 seeked slowest of the measured codecs.
SC-22.value: an H.264 source in every set; VP9 never the default
SC-22.label: measured
SC-22.method: Played and seeked H.264, HEVC, VP9 and AV1 clips in headless Chromium builds with and without hardware decode and in WebKit.
SC-22.remeasure: Check canPlayType and seek times for each codec in the browsers you support.

SC-N0.claim: When scroll progress is smoothed, a time constant keeps the result independent of the refresh rate, unlike a fixed fraction per frame.
SC-N0.value: time-based smoothing with a time constant of about 100 ms, or none
SC-N0.label: inferred
SC-N0.method: Derived from the convergence of per-frame smoothing at different refresh rates.
SC-N0.remeasure: Compare settle times of both smoothing forms at 60 and 120 Hz.

PV-4.claim: A product film's start image is identical to its frame 0, while a separately composed still differs clearly; the video is revealed only after it has presented a frame.
PV-4.value: start image SSIM at least 0.99 against frame 0; a composed still scored about 0.97
PV-4.label: measured
PV-4.method: Compared public start images with the first frame of their films using SSIM.
PV-4.remeasure: Extract frame 0 with ffmpeg and compare it with the start image using the ssim filter.

ON-2.claim: A long pinned story can run from one progress value, clamped to the scene and computed only while the scene is near the viewport.
ON-2.value: one clamped progress value; work only while the scene is near
ON-2.label: measured
ON-2.method: Stepped the scroll of a public landing page in headless Chromium and read the progress it drives.
ON-2.remeasure: Log a scene's progress while stepping the scroll in a headless browser.

ON-4.claim: Stacked backdrop blur layers over a transformed, filtered stage can drop a software-rendered browser to a few frames per second.
ON-4.value: frame rate falls to a few frames per second in software rendering
ON-4.label: measured
ON-4.method: Counted animation frames per second in software-rendered headless Chromium while the layers were visible.
ON-4.remeasure: Count requestAnimationFrame callbacks per second with the blur on screen in a software-rendered browser.

TQ-1.claim: GSAP is free for websites and apps, including commercial work, under its own no-charge licence, which is not an open-source licence and forbids use inside competing no-code animation builders.
TQ-1.value: free for sites and apps; not open source
TQ-1.label: documented
TQ-1.remeasure: Read the licence page again; its terms can change.

TQ-14.claim: CSS scroll-driven animations run in Chromium and Safari but only in Firefox's preview builds, so they are not Baseline.
TQ-14.value: Chrome 115, Safari 26; Firefox preview only; not Baseline
TQ-14.label: measured
TQ-14.method: Queried the browser compatibility data and web-features status.
TQ-14.remeasure: Look up animation-timeline in MDN's compatibility tables.

TQ-23.claim: GSAP with ScrollTrigger adds about 45 KB gzipped to a bundle; native CSS scroll timelines add nothing.
TQ-23.value: GSAP with ScrollTrigger about 44.9 KB gzipped
TQ-23.label: measured
TQ-23.method: Bundled the packages with esbuild and measured gzip -9 sizes.
TQ-23.remeasure: Bundle the same imports and measure gzip -9 size.

TQ-N0.claim: Scrubbing cost tracks keyframe spacing: short GOPs of 5 to 10 frames seek far faster than a long GOP, and an image sequence costs several times the bytes of a long-GOP file.
TQ-N0.value: GOP 5-10; an image sequence about 3.7 times a long-GOP file
TQ-N0.label: measured
TQ-N0.method: Encoded one synthetic clip at several GOP lengths and as an image sequence and measured seeks and sizes.
TQ-N0.remeasure: Encode one clip at GOP 6 and at the encoder default and time random seeks.
